stage1.impression: A shopfront seen from the pavement at night: a red horn pair on a plinth in the window, empty-looking dark shelves on both walls, coloured pendants, and a hard-edged blue rectangle across the middle of the glass. It reads as a clean CG showroom, not a photograph: the shelves are nearly bare, the glass has no believable reflections, the ceiling and the back are crushed black, and the pavement is the brightest thing in the frame. A magazine would see a generic, unopened shop, not a specific place someone would walk into.

blocking_9: The hard-edged blue rectangle on the glass (about x 555-1115, y 318-470) is gone, or turned into a soft, warm, believable reflection
Frame lum_median 22-50 (now 11.6) with the pavement no longer the brightest large area (now median 172 against an interior around 10-20)
The speaker region reads as the hero at lum_median >= 45 (now 19), its horns and edges lit by the window spots, not only by their own glow
The shelves are stocked like a shop that is open: records face-out, lamps, cards and boxes on every tier, not two or three tiers of spines and empty boards
Signs of life: glasses or a bottle on the bar, a record out of its sleeve on the table, a coat, or a figure behind the glass
The back of the room and the ceiling hold detail (region 350-930 x 200-420 now 54 % crushed), with visible pools and falloff from the spots and a little haze
Glass that reads as glass: faint reflection of the street lamp and the pavement, a soft sheen, not an absent pane
Floor and pavement surfaces at 1:1 read as real concrete and stone, not flat grey and a regular CG tile grid

defects.what: Hard-edged blue rectangle across the glass (edge 10-90 width 2 px on the right side); it lifts the shelves inside it to blue (b_median 22 > r 15, crush 0 %) while just below the same shelves are 66 % crushed. Reads as a compositing error.
Pavement is the brightest large area of the frame (lum_median 172, r 208) and a uniform beige tile grid; it pulls the eye away from the window and reads as CG paving.
Back of the room and drapes crushed (crush_pct 54 %, median 2.1) over about 13 % of the frame; the felt, bar back and listening room do not read.
Ceiling and beams a near-black band with no light on them; a third of the top of the frame carries nothing.
Speaker pair median 19, below the 45 the hero needs; the horns are dark, the window spots barely register on the acrylic faces and edges.
Left shelves: three upper tiers empty except small white cards; only the bottom tier holds records. Reads as an unstocked fit-out.
Right shelves: mostly empty boards with a few coloured lamps and coins; a sparse showroom, not a record shop.
The sill/plinth band in front of the glass is a featureless black slab with no edge or reflection, so the pane and its frame do not read.
The floor is a flat, even grey with no pools or sheen from the spots; it reads as a CG plane.
Pendants in red, blue, amber, violet: saturated colour outside the window pair competes with the hero (fixed product tints, see out_of_scope).
No sign of life anywhere: no people, glasses, open records or coats.

changes.problem: A hard-edged blue rectangle sits across the middle of the glass and reads as a render fault.

evidence.measured: b_median 22 > r_median 15 inside, crush 0 %; directly below [1000,480,1100,600] r 3 b 1, crush 66 %; right edge 10-90 width 2 px

change.setting: outside: the source reflected in the shopfront glass (the building opposite / sky panel behind the camera), or the glass's reflection
change.from: a cool, uniformly lit rectangle reflected at full strength with hard edges
change.to: remove it, or make it the building opposite as a dark, warm facade (0-2 windows lit at 2700 K) so the glass reflects only faint warm shapes with soft edges

changes.expected: No blue band; the shelves inside the old rectangle match those below in colour and tone; any reflection is warm and faint.

changes.problem: The interior is far too dark against a bright pavement, so the frame is dim and the eye lands on the paving.

evidence.measured: frame lum_p50 11.6, 70 % of pixels below 40; pavement [0,690,1200,800] median 172

change.setting: street lamp outside; the room's fill
change.to: street lamp 0.05 W/m2, fill 0.25 W/m2 at 2900 K

changes.expected: Pavement drops to a median around 80-110, the interior lifts, the frame median moves into 22-35.

changes.problem: The window pair is not the brightest, clearest thing in the frame.

change.setting: track spots: the window pair 2 x spot
change.to: 60.0 W, cone 26 deg, aimed to graze the horns and the top edges of the cabinets

changes.expected: Horn tops and cabinet edges catch light, the polished edges glow, and the pair reads at a glance from the pavement.

changes.problem: The shelves are nearly empty, so the room reads as an unopened fit-out, not a shop that plays records.

evidence.measured: seen: three upper tiers carry only small white cards; right wall [930,270,1150,640] median 8, mostly bare boards

change.from: records on the bottom tier only
change.to: records face-out on every upper tier (4-6 per bay, mixed sleeves, mostly dark and muted), spines on the lower tiers, a few boxed products and price cards

changes.expected: Both walls read as a stocked record shop; small highlights on sleeves catch the shelf LEDs.

changes.problem: The back of the room, the felt drapes and the ceiling are crushed, so there is no depth or atmosphere.

evidence.measured: lum_median 2.1, crush_pct 53.7 % over 13 % of the frame

change.to: wash 2.0 W/m2 at 2600 K; haze 0.0025 per m

changes.expected: The felt shows its folds, spot cones become faintly visible, and the back holds detail without going grey.

changes.problem: There is no sign of life, so the frame cannot read as a specific place.

evidence.measured: seen: bar and table bare, no glasses, records or people

change.to: two tumblers and a bottle on the bar under its spot, a record out of its sleeve and a sleeve on the table, a coat over a chair, a shop-hours card on the glass

changes.expected: Small, bright highlights on the bar and table; the room reads as open tonight.

changes.problem: The floor and the pavement read as CG planes: flat grey inside, a regular beige tile grid outside.

evidence.measured: floor median 59.7 with no pools; pavement r 208 g 166 b 130, an even grid

change.setting: the floor's tone and sheen; outside: the pavement
change.from: floor #6A645D matte; pavement #45423E rendering bright beige
change.to: floor #5A554F with a low satin sheen (roughness about 0.35) so the spots pool on it; pavement darker and wet-looking (#2E2C29, roughness 0.3) with irregular slab wear

changes.expected: Soft pools and reflections of the speakers and spots on the floor; the pavement recedes and mirrors the window's warm light.

changes.problem: The pair is small in a frame that spends its top quarter on a black ceiling, so it does not stop a passer-by.

evidence.measured: top band lum_median 8.6, no information; speakers fill about 26 % of the width

change.to: position [-3.8, 2.2, 1.35], 40 mm, still level, target at the window pair's horn height

changes.expected: The pair fills about 40 % of the width, less dead ceiling, the shelves frame the pair from both sides.

out_of_scope.request: Reduce the coloured pendants and lamps (red, blue, violet, amber Hemispheres; teal Tropos at the back) so the window pair is the only saturated colour
out_of_scope.why: The products' tints as placed are fixed by the card; the shop shows the line in its tints. It does cost the frame its single-colour read.

out_of_scope.request: A mullion, door or sign on the shopfront to make the pane read as glass and the shop as a named place
out_of_scope.why: The shopfront is part of the plan (A-401); only the glass finish and lettering-like small props may change.
